summary: TSV playback index generation failing and SIEM connector intermittent healthcheck 502s for FinSight Capital
description:
Issue summary:
Customer FinSight Capital reports they requested a TSV-formatted activity playback index with per-session anchors for e-discovery. The customer's AWS Lambda forwarder (v1.7.2) occasionally drops records and the Redwood SIEM connector shows intermittent 502 healthcheck responses during bursts.

Impact:
- Customer cannot complete compliance replay tests for a regulatory audit window; they have a deadline next week.
- Missing entries observed for ~0.1-0.5% of session IDs in playback index; evidence package rejected by customer security team.

Environment:
- Customer account: finsight-prod
- Customer tier: enterprise
- Forwarder: aws-lambda-forwarder v1.7.2 (configured as Kinesis->Lambda->Redwood-HTTP)
- SIEM connector: rwd-siem-connector v2.3.0 deployed in prod-us-east-1

Steps to reproduce (as provided by customer):
1) Trigger audit replay job for window 2026-03-07T00:00:00Z to 2026-03-07T04:00:00Z
2) Lambda forwarder packages payloads as gzipped TSV batches and POSTs to /v1/audit/import
3) Connector healthcheck shows 200 at steady state, but during bursts returns 502
4) Playback index generation (internal job) completes with warnings; index contains gaps for session anchors

Logs and snippets (customer-provided):
- lambda logs show partial write responses: "WARN write partial: 2026-03-07T02:12:03Z status=202 bytes=614"
- connector logs show: "ERROR healthcheck probe failed: upstream read timeout (502)" repeated at 02:12:04Z
- sample TSV row provided (redacted): "session_id\tsrc_ip\tevent_ts\taction\tuser_id"

Customer request:
- Produce a reproducible TSV playback index that preserves per-session ordering and includes resume tokens.
- Verify SIEM connector health stability under burst load and provide signed timestamped manifest for the evidence bundle.

Requested deliverables:
- Signed manifest (RFC3161 or equivalent) for the playback slice
- Guidance or patch for Lambda forwarder to avoid partial writes (preferred immediate workaround)
- Connector config tweaks to reduce 502s during ingestion bursts

Attachments from customer: list of 3 gzipped sample batches, sample playback index (with gaps), and CloudWatch traces (S3 link).
comments: [2026-03-10 10:15] Aisha Thompson (Support): Acknowledged receipt of evidence and escalated to ingest team. First response provided to customer with request for CloudWatch Trace IDs and one raw batch.

[2026-03-10 12:46] Marcus Li (SRE): Reproduced partial write locally by replaying gzipped TSV batches. Observed connector's ingest worker returns 502 when payload size > 512KB and concurrent inflight requests > 8.
[2026-03-11 08:02] Elena Park (Customer Success): Noted customer's audit deadline 2026-03-14. Asked for ETA on signed manifest and temporary mitigation.

[2026-03-11 14:30] Marcus Li (SRE): Proposed temporary workaround: switch forwarder to NDJSON newline-delimited events and reduce batch size to 256KB; also enable connector env var READ_TIMEOUT_MS=120000. Asked customer to test with one replay window.
[2026-03-12 09:12] FinSight Capital (Customer): Confirmed they tested NDJSON forwarder with smaller batches; gaps reduced to 0.01%. Requested signed manifest and a small patch release for forwarder.

[2026-03-12 15:45] Marcus Li (SRE): Patch PR opened (github.com/redwood/integrations-lambda/pull/412) to add optional NDJSON mode and automatic batch-splitting. Preparing signed manifest and instructions.
investigation_notes: Checked ingestion metrics on prod-us-east-1 between 2026-03-07T02:00 and 2026-03-07T03:00: spike to 1.8x baseline TPS coincident with 502s.
Connector's worker thread pool was saturating due to large compressed payloads requiring decompress CPU; discovered blocking on gzip streams leading to upstream read timeouts.
Lambda forwarder uses chunked gzip with content-length omitted; connector misinterprets chunk sizes causing partial-write semantics in our SDK.
Reproduced issue by sending gzipped TSV batches with 700KB payloads concurrently (8+) and saw ~0.3% dropped sessions in generated index.
Signed manifest generation is implemented in internal tool rwd-audit-tool v0.9; can produce RFC3161 timestamps but needs fine-grained event counts per-batch for customer's legal team.
next_steps: - Provide customer with signed manifest for the provided slice by 2026-03-13 (Marcus).
- Ship hotfix to aws-lambda-forwarder to add NDJSON mode and automatic batch splitting (PR #412) and cut v1.7.3 (Engineering).
- Apply connector env var tweak (READ_TIMEOUT_MS=120000) behind a canary and monitor 1 hour at 2x baseline traffic (SRE).
- Provide customer runbook snippet for replay (Support/CS).
resolution: Workaround provided: Customer switched forwarder to NDJSON and reduced batch size; observed substantive reduction in missing session anchors. Hotfix PR opened for forwarder and signed RFC3161 manifest delivered for the provided slice. Connector timeout adjusted in canary; monitoring underway. Final resolution pending hotfix rollout and 24h monitoring.
